_note: Debate topics. 'trigger' topics start by themselves when the country is in that state; the rest are started by news, parties or events. Lean runs from the axis's left side (-100) to its right side (+100).

TOPICS.title: The cost of living
TOPICS.text: Prices keep climbing faster than wages. Everyone has a theory about whose fault it is.

TOPICS.title: Where are the jobs?
TOPICS.text: Factories are cutting shifts and young people are leaving for the cities, or for abroad.

TOPICS.title: How many is too many?
TOPICS.text: Arrivals are at a record high. Some towns say they can't cope; employers say they can't do without them.

TOPICS.title: Is the border safe?
TOPICS.text: Trouble across the border has people asking whether the army is ready, and whether it should be.

TOPICS.title: Angry streets
TOPICS.text: Protests most weekends. Commentators argue about whether the anger is a symptom or the problem.

TOPICS.title: Who is a real Cranebonian?
TOPICS.text: A row over a school textbook has turned into a fight about who belongs here and what the flag means.

TOPICS.title: Who pays for the state?
TOPICS.text: The deficit is back in the headlines. Cut spending, or tax the people who can afford it?

TOPICS.title: The family under pressure
TOPICS.text: Fewer marriages, fewer children, more of everything else. Is that freedom, or decline?

TOPICS.title: Should we arm up?
TOPICS.text: Neighbours are spending on tanks. Cranebonistan is spending on pensions. Which is the mistake?

TOPICS.title: Hospitals and schools
TOPICS.text: Waiting lists are long and classrooms are full. More money, or less waste?

TOPICS.title: A fair day's pay
TOPICS.text: Profits are up, pay is flat. Unions want a share; owners warn that jobs will move abroad.

TOPICS.title: Who gets to come in?
TOPICS.text: A new visa scheme has split the country between those who see workers and those who see strangers.

TOPICS.title: Clean out the capital
TOPICS.text: Another minister, another envelope. Fix the system, or tear it down?
